problems.statement: The fallback is used when the model directory has no `tokenizer.json`, when the Rust tokenizer fails to load, or when `USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER` or `VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS` is enabled.
problems.code_says: Wrong for the case "the Rust tokenizer fails to load". `make_tokenizer` falls back only when `hf_tokenizer.handle` is null. `make_huggingface_tokenizer` returns `make_shared<huggingface_tokenizer_handle>(...)`, so the handle is never null. The constructor of that handle is `noexcept`. When `tokenizer_from_file` fails, the constructor logs `Failed to load HuggingFace tokenizer from <path>` and returns with a null `tokenizer_ptr`. So the test in `make_tokenizer` is always true when `tokenizer.json` exists. The warning `Failed to load HuggingFace tokenizer` and the Python fallback after it are never reached on this path. The process keeps the Rust handle, and `encode` then logs `HuggingFace tokenizer is null` and returns no tokens. The other three cases hold: no `tokenizer.json` (line 1899), `VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS` (line 2193) and `USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER` (line 2197). This finding comes from reading the code. No run confirmed it, because this task forbids runs.
problems.corrected_cell: Names the program that the Python fallback tokenizer runs as a child process to read the vocabulary and to encode text. In a Nix dev shell, `make gen/tokenize_py` copies this file to `gen/tokenize_py`. The fallback is used when the model directory has no `tokenizer.json`, or when `USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER` or `VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS` is enabled. A `tokenizer.json` that the Rust tokenizer cannot load does not start the fallback. `make_tokenizer` has a branch for that case, but `make_huggingface_tokenizer` always returns a handle, so the branch never runs. The warning `Falling back to slow tokenizer script <path>` shows the path in effect. The Nix dev shell sets it. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` also sets it, for the command of an LSF job that `bin/dice-lsf-submit` sent from a Nix dev shell.

problems.statement: If the path does not exist, the program aborts with `Python tokenizer script <path> not found`.
problems.code_says: Imprecise. The sentence misses the condition. The check is a `TRON_ASSERT` in the constructor of the fallback tokenizer. A wrong path has no effect while no model uses the fallback. The same check covers the default `bin/tokenize_py`. So an unset variable gives the same abort when the working directory has no `bin/tokenize_py`. The row places the sentence before "Unset:", so a reader takes it for set values only. An empty value counts as unset in the C++ code and in the `make` rule.
problems.corrected_cell: Path of an executable tokenizer program. The text is used as given. An empty value counts as unset. Unset: the programs run `bin/tokenize_py`, relative to their working directory. The code checks the path only when the fallback tokenizer starts. If the path in effect does not exist then, the program aborts with `Python tokenizer script <path> not found`. This holds for the default path too. In a Nix dev shell, `make gen/tokenize_py` stops with an error when the variable is unset or empty.

problems.statement: The Nix dev shell sets it.
problems.code_says: Imprecise. The Nix dev shell is not the only setter. `bin/dice-lsf-runner` sets it for the command of an LSF job when the envelope field `runtime.nix_tokenize_py` is true. `bin/dice-lsf-submit` sets that field when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is set and the payload is a Dice-aware command. The runner builds the Nix tokenizer package on the worker and sets the variable to `<job directory>/nix-tokenize-py/bin/tokenize_py`.

notes: Short version: 8 of the 10 rows are correct, 1 row is imprecise (`GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`) and 1 row is wrong (`TRON_TOKENIZE_PY`). The wrong row names a trigger of the Python fallback tokenizer that the code cannot reach. Method: for each variable I ran `git grep` on the name and on its constant or helper, then read every read site, every set site and the callers. I built nothing and ran nothing, so every finding comes from reading the code at the staged checkout. Details. (1) `TRON_TOKENIZE_PY`: the branch `Failed to load HuggingFace tokenizer` in `make_tokenizer` exists, so the row matches the intent of the code, but `make_huggingface_tokenizer` never returns a null handle, so the branch is dead. This may be a code defect that is worth a separate issue. A test that loads a model directory with a broken `tokenizer.json` and checks which tokenizer answers would confirm or reject the finding. (2) `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT`: the gap is only the `Tron` cell. The rows `GITHUB_RUN_ID` and `GITHUB_JOB` are outside this sample, but the same test script lines set and remove those names too, and both rows also say `Reads`. (3) Details that I saw and did not grade as problems, because they do not change what a reader does: `rinzler_mock`, `rinzler_host` and the test `t_rinzler` also read `RZ_RUNFILE_DIR`; an empty `DICE_LOG_PATH` counts as unset, and a test-configured Dice client also resolves it to create the parent directory; the `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` row does not say that `prime_hf_models.py` only writes the value in the `ci` field of its `cache_context` log line, that `publish_regional.py` fails with `KeyError` when the name is unset, or that `background-check.sh` exits with its usage text when `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is set and the attempt is not a number; `make` can take `REMOTE` from `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` before it decides to run `bin/bsub-build`; `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` has a shell variable named `GIT_SHA7` that is not exported and is not the environment variable of the row.
